section_1.content: Review prerequisite (standard 2D/3D vectors). Introduce the idea that vectors aren't just arrows, but objects that follow specific 'rules of engagement' (addition and scalar multiplication).
section_1.example: Visual: An arrow (v) transforms into a function (f(x)) and a 2x2 matrix, both following the same vector addition rules.

section_2.title: The Eight Axioms: Defining the Space
section_2.content: Introduce the formal structure of a Vector Space (V) over a field (F). Focus on closure, associativity, commutativity, identity, and inverses.
section_2.example: A 'Robot Logic' checklist: If two states are combined (Addition) and scaled (Multiplication), do they remain in the original 'Robot World' (Closure)?

section_3.title: Non-Traditional Examples: Beyond Arrows
section_3.content: Demonstrate that unusual sets can be vector spaces if they obey the 8 axioms. This highlights the power of abstraction.
section_3.example: The 'Polynomial Garden': Showing that the set of all polynomials of degree ≤ 2 behaves exactly like vectors in 3D space, represented by coordinates [a, b, c].

section_4.title: Visualization: Mapping Abstract Spaces
section_4.content: Explain how abstract spaces can be visualized via 'isomorphism'—mapping complex abstract structures onto familiar 3D grids.
section_4.example: Animation: A sound wave (complex) being mapped onto a coordinate grid representing frequency amplitudes, showing how abstract spaces help us solve real-world signal problems.

section_5.title: Summary & Application
section_5.content: Recap: An abstract vector space is a 'set with rules'. Application: Why this matters for Machine Learning (feature spaces) and Quantum Physics.
section_5.example: A neural network character 'classifying' different animal features as vectors in a high-dimensional space, proving that abstraction leads to powerful predictive tools.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Right side alignment
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualization: Mapping Abstract Spaces", [
            "- Abstract spaces can be mapped visually.",
            "- Isomorphisms translate complex structures to grids.",
            "- Sound waves map onto coordinate systems."
        ])
        
        # Setup Axes for coordinate mapping
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"color": "#FFFFFF"})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Create(axes))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        dot = Dot(color="#FF6347")
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "C3")
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF6347"), FadeIn(dot))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        grid_lines = VGroup(*[Line(axes.c2p(-2, i), axes.c2p(2, i), color="#32CD32") for i in range(-2, 3)])
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"), Create(grid_lines))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Right side alignment
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Non-Traditional Examples: Beyond Arrows", [
            "Unusual sets can form vector spaces.",
            "Polynomials act like coordinate-based vectors.",
            "Degree-two polynomials behave identically to 3D space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display function set labeled #FFFFFF
        set_label = Text("Set P: {a + bx + cx^2}", font_size=24, color=WHITE)

        self.play(Create(matrix_grid))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#40E0D0")
        self.wait(2)
